A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KG-ViP research work. All 14 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.4, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original KG-ViP experiments on FVQA 2.0+ and MVQA, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, architecture evaluations, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 4, Tables 1–5, Figure 3, and the appendix case studies in Figure 4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same graph construction, two-stage retrieval, cross-modal graph fusion, optional refinement, and answer-generation procedures. The appendix prompts are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same FVQA 2.0+ and MVQA benchmarks, covering fact-based VQA and movie-domain reasoning. No dataset, domain, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Zero-shot, CoT, Fine-Tuning, CCoT, NaiveRAG, FilterRAG, and LLM-RA. Comparator membership in the supplementary comparisons also remains unchanged; the newly cited Xiong et al. work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix A.1 retain the same metrics, models, refinement setting, and baseline configurations. Evaluation sample counts remain 2,820 for FVQA 2.0+ and 1,433 for MVQA.

E4.justification: The fusion/refinement, retrieval-mode, pruning, vision-encoder, and architecture analyses are unchanged in Tables 2–5 and Figure 3. Appendix A.3 and Figure 4 retain the same three qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point-estimate results without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–4 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports KG-ViP DeepSeek-V3.2 LLM-J scores of 60.40 on FVQA 2.0+ and 35.44 on MVQA in both versions.

T1.justification: The graph and subgraph definitions and cross-graph alignment similarity formula in Section 3 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems, proofs, or formal derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about complementary scene and commonsense graphs, the unified KG-ViP framework, and its empirical superiority.

C2.justification: Interpretations of fusion, pruning, retrieval, and encoder results remain unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning scene-graph parsing quality and updating the offline commonsense graph.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendices A.1–A.4 retain the same hardware, software, model identifiers, LoRA and retrieval settings, benchmark construction details, and prompt templates. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: v3 replaces the unresolved introductory citation '?' with Xiong et al. (2025) and adds its bibliography entry, 'Deliberate reasoning in language models as structure-aware planning with an accurate world model.' The related-work discussion and research positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introductory citation is repaired and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The substantive prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: The citation addition produces limited column and page reflow, shifting Table 6 and Figure 4 and splitting the scene-graph prompt across pages 13–14. Figure content, table structures, captions, and legends remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs an unresolved citation in the opening paragraph and supplies an identifiable bibliography entry, modestly improving editorial completeness. The scientific claims, experimental evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information are unchanged, so the overall gain is small.
